findings.evidence: “Define reusable token categories explicitly—not just example values—including color, typography ... and spacing” and “Ship a short component documentation guide” repeat familiar design-system scaffolding. The workflow's pilot selection and compatibility contracts provide stronger expert delta than these routine category and documentation lists.
findings.fix: Compress the standard token-category and documentation inventories into short output requirements. Keep the substantive guidance on selecting an adopter, validating theme-state pairs, limiting escape hatches, and preserving token meaning.

findings.evidence: “Component source scaffold: `templates/component-template.tsx`” has no framework-specific loading condition, although the skill also supports token-only and non-React design-system work.
findings.fix: Load templates/component-template.tsx only when implementing a React component scaffold; explicitly skip it for token-only deliverables and other frameworks.

findings.evidence: “All Atoms Complete,” “Key Molecules Complete,” and “Core Organisms Complete” are unconditional pre-launch gates, followed by mandatory Figma and NPM publication. This conflicts with the main workflow's instruction to avoid components without a real reuse case and immediate adopter.
findings.fix: Make the checklist scope-dependent, allow justified N/A entries, and gate release on the chosen pilot and supported distribution channels. Treat component inventories, publication platforms, and numeric budgets as project decisions rather than universal requirements.

findings.evidence: The token eval asks to “propose semantic design tokens and a light/dark CSS-variable mapping,” but its assertions check categories, mappings, and stated contrast thresholds rather than the workflow's alias-cycle, missing-target, or failing-contrast branches.
findings.fix: Add a token fixture with a cycle, a missing alias target, and an actual failing foreground/background pair. Assert that each defect is identified and corrected or explicitly blocks component implementation.

findings.evidence: “Can you audit a modal for focus handling and screen-reader behavior?” is labeled should_trigger=true without any shared-system context, despite the skill's stated scope of creating or evolving shared contracts rather than standalone accessibility help.
findings.fix: Label the standalone modal audit as a near-miss negative, or rewrite the positive to specify reviewing a shared modal primitive used across the design system.

findings.evidence: “Object.assign(ForwardedComponent, { Header, Body })” exposes compound children whose implementations return div elements, while ForwardedComponent renders a button. Following the apparent Component.Header/Component.Body composition produces invalid button content rather than a sound reusable component hierarchy.
findings.fix: Keep the button scaffold limited to valid phrasing content and remove its Header/Body members, or provide a separate non-interactive container scaffold for compound Header/Body composition. Validate the resulting DOM structure in a rendered example.
